request.prompt:
A rider travels this weekend from Delancey St-Essex St to Franklin St using only the services and free transfers shown on this map. Walking between stations joined on the map counts as a transfer, and the trip ends when a train arrives at Franklin St itself. They want the fewest transfers and, among those trips, the fewest station stops. Which services do they ride, in order? If more than one service runs between the same two stations on a leg, any of them is accepted. Answer as a JSON list of route letters or numbers, for example ["A", "7"].

Answer the question using the image. Think it through, then give the answer as a JSON list of names exactly as written on the map, in order, e.g. ["A", "7"].
End your reply with a final line of the form:
FINAL ANSWER: <answer>

content:
The fewest-transfer trip is two transfers, riding J, then R, then 1.

1. **J** from Delancey St-Essex St west to Bowery, then south to Canal St (the J/R/6/N/Q station).
2. Transfer at Canal St to **R**, which runs south through City Hall and Cortlandt St to Whitehall St-South Ferry.
3. Transfer at Whitehall St-South Ferry (a free transfer on the map) to **1**, which runs north through Rector St, WTC Cortlandt and Chambers St to Franklin St.

Franklin St is served only by the 1 line, and the map shows no free transfer onto the 1 line from the Delancey services. The only connections into the 1 line are at South Ferry (from R) and at Chambers St (from the 2/3, which don't run in this section on weekends). So no one-transfer trip exists, and I found no other two-transfer option with fewer stops.

FINAL ANSWER: ["J", "R", "1"]
